title: Polynomial-Time Recursive Pair Decoding
statement: Let $b,d:\{0,1\}^*\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{0,1\}^*$ be functions such that the maps sending a bit string $p$ to $b(\pi_1(p),\pi_2(p))$ and to $d(\pi_1(p),\pi_2(p))$ are polynomial-time computable, where $\pi_1,\pi_2$ are the total projections associated with the self-delimiting pair encoding. For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, the map obtained by starting at level zero with $p\mapsto b(\pi_1(p),\pi_2(p))$ and, at each successive level, pairing the preceding-level value on $\pi_1(p)$ with $d(\pi_1(p),\pi_2(p))$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: The map $p\mapsto b(\pi_1(p),\pi_2(p))$ is polynomial-time computable
The map $p\mapsto d(\pi_1(p),\pi_2(p))$ is polynomial-time computable
